items.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001
items.q: That’s where Eartha Kitt came from, Robert Clary. He was called Leonard Sillman. He would get all these young people, he would find these “New Faces.”

ctx.x: Smart Affairs? He used to sing. That’s where Eartha Kitt came from, Robert Clary. He was called Leonard Sillman. He would get all these young people, he would find these “New Faces.” He called them like “New Faces” of 1949, then 1950, and every year he would audition and then he would put a show together and take them around the country. Eartha Kitt — all these people came from that guy, that “New Faces.” Robert Clary, a couple of those guys. But anyway, we auditioned for him. And Tommy was our accompanist. And…
What were a couple of the tunes that you would have done in that act?
